SigMod.notes: The README writes the decision as !(v1<Cmp1 XOR v2<Cmp2) XOR v3<Cmp3 and describes the menu as inverting a 'less than' test; the installed code compares with 'at or above' and takes !(b1 XOR b2) XOR b3 from those results, which is the same shape with the sense of each test turned around. The README does not mention the Mod/SR/Seq switch, the PosO knob or the SR output, which are all in this build. The In jack carries whatever signal you patch, so it has no family.

Moves every ant on by the number of steps set by Steps

Ant.notes: Param 4 is declared in the code but has no control on the panel, so it has no line and no tag; a number-of-ants knob for it is commented out and the setting lives in the menu instead.

lines: Billiard simulation for sequencing: balls bounce around a table, and their positions and collisions come out as polyphonic voltages
Sets how many balls are in play, 1 to 16; changing it starts the scene again
The coefficient of restitution, 0 to 2; at 1 collisions lose no speed and above 1 the balls speed up with every collision
Sets the radius of every ball while the R input is unpatched, 0.05 to 0.15 of the table
Sets the radius of each ball separately, one channel per ball, -5V to 5V spanning 0.05 to 0.15 of the table

A 1ms trigger on a ball's channel when that ball hits a wall

Eight step sequencer where every step carries a probability of being skipped, with glide and reset per step
Each rising edge moves on, skipping any step the probabilities skip over
A rising edge restarts the sequence, reseeds the random generator from the Seed input and blocks the clock for 1ms
A rising edge restarts this sequencer and every UnoE chained to its right at the same moment
Picks the order: forwards, backwards or pendulum

Sets the voltage its step puts out, within the range picked in the menu
Sets its CV knob from the voltage on the matching channel, one channel per step, while a cable is patched
The chance that its step plays rather than being skipped, 0 to 100%
Sets the step chances, one channel per step, 0V for a step that is always skipped through to 1V for a step that always plays
While on, its step holds the gate high instead of passing the clock, which glides into the next step

The voltage of the step the sequence has reached
Follows the clock while the step is playing, and stays high while a step with Glide on is playing
Carries 10V on the channel of the step the sequence has reached while its gate is high, eight channels wide

Uno.notes: The Seed input's tooltip reads Direction, which looks like a copied name: the code uses it as the random seed.

lines: Expander that plays the step voltages, probabilities, glides and resets of the Uno to its left on its own clock; it goes immediately to the right of Uno, and another UnoE can be chained to its right
Each rising edge moves on, skipping any step the probabilities of the module to the left skip over
A rising edge restarts this sequence, reseeds its random generator from the Seed input and blocks the clock for 1ms
Picks the order for this sequence: forwards, backwards or pendulum
Sets the seed the random generator takes on a reset, so the same run of skips comes back; the seed is the voltage divided by ten and zero gives a fresh run
The voltage of the step this sequence has reached, taken from the CV knobs of the module to the left
Follows the clock while the step is playing, and stays high while a step with Glide on is playing
Carries 10V on the channel of the step this sequence has reached while its gate is high, eight channels wide
Klee style sequencer: a sixteen place shift register of bits circulates on every clock, and the steps whose bit is set add their knob voltages together and fire three gate buses
Sets the voltage its step adds to its sum while its bit is set, within the range picked in the menu
Sets its CV knob from the voltage patched here, overriding both the knob and the poly CV input
Sets the bit its step is given the next time the pattern is loaded
Sends its step to bus 1, bus 2 or bus 3
Switches on a feedback tap at its step, whose bit is exclusive-ORed into the bit read into the register

Loads the pattern buttons into the shift register

While on, the pattern is loaded into the register whenever bus 1 goes active
Shifts the register on by one place by hand
Each rising edge shifts the register on by one place

Switches Random on above 5V and off below
The chance of reading in a one while Random is on, 0 to 1

Sets the pattern bits the next load will use, one channel per step, above 0V for a one

Switches the feedback taps on above 5V and off below

Sets the voltage its step puts out, within the range picked in the menu

Returns to the first step and brings back the last stored sequence, dropping every variation and modulation

The voltage whose bits are read as the four step counts
Slews every cell output, from an instant jump at zero to a slow glide at full
While on, a byte is taken as one run of that many steps; while off, its eight bits are walked one at a time, a single step for each bit that is set
While on, a cell visited by the walk is switched rather than counted, and the outputs are either off or full; while off, visits are counted and scaled by Scale
While off, the input voltage is rounded up to a whole volt before its bits are read
While off, a cell's counted value is held at its top rather than wrapping around when the scale takes it past the top
While on, the cell outputs run 0-10V; while off they run -5V to 5V
Carries the value of its cell of the grid, one output per cell
Swen.notes: Ported from the QWELK N.E.W.S module. The Round, Clamp, Mode, GateMode and Uni buttons are read inverted in the code, so the behaviour described here is the one each button gives in the state named. The IN jack takes whatever voltage you want read as bits, so it has no family.

lines: Sixteen trigger tracks written as hexadecimal text, four steps to a character, with 100 patterns and a chance of adding or dropping triggers
Each rising edge moves every track on by one step
A rising edge sends every track back to its first step
Selects the pattern, 0.1V per pattern over 0-10V; while it is patched the pattern cannot be picked by hand unless Edit is on
Picks which of the 100 patterns is played and edited
While on, the pattern is picked by hand and a cable in the pattern input no longer moves the selection
Copies all sixteen hex lines of the current pattern
Writes the copied hex lines into the current pattern
Pushes the patterns after the current one along by one place and empties the current one; the hundredth pattern is lost
Removes the current pattern and pulls every later pattern back one place
At 100% its track plays its written triggers; below that each written trigger has that chance of firing, and above it each step with no written trigger has the extra chance of firing
The chance that its track fires an inverted trigger on a step where nothing is written, 0 to 100%
Runs its track; while it is off that track fires nothing on either output
A 10ms trigger on a track's channel for each step that fires, sixteen channels wide
Carries 10V on a track's channel while the step it has reached fires, sixteen channels wide
Passes the clock through on a track's channel while the step it has reached fires, sixteen channels wide, despite its tooltip reading Inverted Clock
A 10ms trigger on a track's channel for each step that fires an inverted trigger, sixteen channels wide
Passes the clock through on a track's channel while the step it has reached is not firing, sixteen channels wide
Note — each line is typed as hexadecimal digits, one digit to four steps, and a star in place of a digit draws a new random digit every time it is read
Note — the number keys 1 to 9 move the cursor to that line of the pattern
Menu — ShowLights hides or shows the step lights over the text lines
Menu — Clock In Delay holds the clock back by up to ten samples, to let a pattern change arrive first
Menu — Random opens a density slider, and Random length from and Random length to set how many digits a randomised line gets
Menu — Randomize Pattern writes new random lines into the current pattern; Initialize Pattern empties it
HexSeqP2.notes: Output 2 carries the gated clock but its tooltip reads Inverted Clock, because the code configures that name onto the wrong output; output 4, the real inverted clock, has no tooltip at all. The clock and reset inputs have no tooltips either.

lines: Triadex Muse emulator: a 31 bit shift register clocked into a repeating pattern, with four sliders picking the note and four picking how the pattern grows
Picks what the ones bit of the note number follows: OFF, ON, one of the counter divisions C1/2 to C8, or one of the 31 register bits B1 to B31
Picks what the twos bit of the note number follows, from the same list of forty
Picks what the fours bit of the note number follows, from the same list of forty
Picks what the eights bit of the note number follows, from the same list of forty
Picks the first of the four taps that are exclusive-ORed together to make the bit read into the register
Picks the second of the four taps that are exclusive-ORed together to make the bit read into the register
Picks the third of the four taps that are exclusive-ORed together to make the bit read into the register
Picks the fourth of the four taps that are exclusive-ORed together to make the bit read into the register
Selects what that slider follows, a quarter of a volt per position over the list of forty, and overrides the slider while patched; the jacks under the X and Y sliders carry each other's tooltip names
Each rising edge clocks the register on; with PWMClock set in the menu the falling edge is used as well
Steps the register on by hand
A rising edge clears the register and restarts the counters
Clears the register and restarts the counters
Sets the eight note scale the Note output uses, one channel per note, 0-1V read as twelve semitones; with nothing patched it is a major scale
The note number played as a pitch, taken from the scale with the top bit adding an octave
A 1ms trigger whenever the note number changes
Multiplies the note number, 0 to 16, before it reaches the CV output, 0 to 1
The note number times the level; at 10/16V per step it addresses sixteen steps over 0-10V
Menu — PWMClock takes the falling edge of the clock as the half step, so the module runs at the clock rate; turned off, only rising edges count and the clock has to run at double speed
TME.notes: The tooltips of the X and Y inputs are swapped in the code: the jack under the X slider reads Y and the one under Y reads X.

lines: Sequencer played by dragging the mouse over a 32 by 32 pad, recording what is played into one of 100 patterns and playing it back on a clock
Picks which of the four clock inputs drives the module
Selects the clock input, 2.5V per input, and overrides the clock selector while patched
One of the four clock inputs; only the selected one is read, and every step of playing and recording happens on its rising edge
Picks which of the four scales the pad is quantised to
Selects the scale, 2.5V per scale, and overrides the scale selector while patched
Plays the current pattern back from its start, with the gate high until it ends
A rising edge plays the current pattern back from its start
Picks which of the 100 patterns is recorded into and played back
Selects the pattern, 0.1V per pattern over 0-10V; while it is patched the pattern cannot be picked by hand unless Lock is on
While on, the pattern is picked by hand and a cable in the pattern input no longer moves the selection
Takes the note, velocity and gate from the X, Y and Gate inputs in place of the mouse, so another module can play and record into the pad
Sets the row, and so the note, while Mode is on, 0-10V across the 32 rows
Sets the column, and so the velocity, while Mode is on, 0-10V across the 32 columns
Starts and stops a note while Mode is on: above 5V is a note held, below is silence, and the recording of a pattern runs while it is high
Shifts the whole output up or down in octaves, -4 to 4
Sets the octave shift, one octave per volt
Shifts the whole output up in semitones, 0 to 11
Sets the semitone shift, 1.2 semitones per volt
The note under the play position as a pitch, quantised to the selected scale and shifted by the Octave and Semitone controls
The column of the play position as a voltage, 0-10V across the pad, which is the velocity of the note
Carries 10V while a note is held and while a pattern is playing back
A 10ms trigger each time the note changes
Note — pressing and dragging on the pad plays and records, and clicking a note in one of the four scale strips takes it out of that scale or puts it back
Note — while the pointer is over the pad the keys z, x, c and v pick the clock input and a, s, d and f pick the scale
Turns one voltage into 32 gates, taken from the bits of that voltage or from a random number seeded by it
The voltage the gates are made from, 0-10V, or -5V to 5V when BiPolar is on
With a cable patched here the gates are made on each rising edge and held between edges; with nothing patched they follow the input continuously
Shifts the read range to -5V to 5V in place of 0-10V
Picks how the gates are made: ieee takes the raw bits of the input as a floating point number, int spreads the input over a 32 bit whole number, rnd seeds one random number with that
Selects the method, one volt per method, and overrides the method switch while patched
The first sixteen bits, one per channel, 10V for a set bit and 0V for a clear one
The last sixteen bits, one per channel, 10V for a set bit and 0V for a clear one
A slider played by the mouse that records the movement and plays it back
Plays the last recorded movement back from its start, holding the gate high until it ends
A rising edge plays the last recorded movement back from its start
The slider position, 0-10V, with the top of the strip at 10V
Carries 10V while the mouse is held on the strip and through a playback, and 0V otherwise
Note — pressing on the strip jumps the slider there and starts a new recording, dragging writes the movement into it, and releasing ends the recording
MC1.notes: Param 1 is declared in the code but has no control on the panel, so it has no line and no tag.

lines: Clock generator with nine outputs, each at its own ratio to the tempo, with its own pulse width and swing
Sets the tempo, 30 to 240 BPM, shown in the display
Sets the tempo as one octave per volt with 0V at 120 BPM, clamped between -2V at 30 BPM and 1V at 240 BPM, and overrides the BPM knob while patched; the README puts 0V at 60 BPM
Carries the tempo as one octave per volt with 0V at 120 BPM
Runs the clocks; while it is off every clock output stays at 0V, and switching it on restarts them all together
Runs the clocks while the voltage here is above 0V
Carries 10V while the clocks are running and 0V while they are stopped
Restarts every clock together and fires the reset output
A rising edge restarts every clock together and fires the reset output
A 1ms trigger whenever the clocks are restarted
Sets the ratio of its clock to the tempo, from sixteen whole notes down to a 128th, shown beside the knob
Sets how far its clock's off beats are pushed late, 0 to 50% of a beat
Sets the pulse width of its clock, 0 to 100% of its period
Sets the pulse width of that clock, 0-10V across the whole range, and overrides the PW knob while patched
Carries its clock, 10V while the pulse is high
Note — the display under the tempo counts the time the clocks have been running, in minutes, seconds and milliseconds
Menu — Accurate times the pulses from a sample count so they do not drift; turned off, each clock runs from its own phase
Menu — Show Time hides or shows the running time under the tempo
Menu — Show Alternative Labels names each ratio as a multiple of the beat, x4 in place of 1/16
PwmClock.notes: The README gives the BPM input as two to the power of the voltage in Hz, which would put 0V at 60 BPM; the installed code multiplies 120 BPM by two to the power of the voltage, so 0V is 120 BPM, 1V is 240 BPM and -2V is 30 BPM.

lines: Binary counter with eight bit outputs, counting up or down by a step amount taken from a polyphonic input
A trigger here adds the step amount to the count, which wraps around after 255
A trigger here subtracts the step amount from the count, which wraps around below zero
A trigger here sets the count to zero and blocks the next increment for 1ms
Sets the step amount as an eight bit number, one channel per bit, a channel above 1V counting as a one; with nothing patched the step is 1
Carries 10V while that bit of the count is set and 0V while it is clear
Carries all eight bits of the count at once, one channel per bit, 10V for a set bit and 0V for a clear one
Converts an input voltage to eight bits and puts each bit out as a gate
The voltage that is converted, 0-10V spanning the eight bit range, or -5V to 5V when BiPolar is on; voltages outside the range are clamped
With a cable patched here the voltage is converted on each rising edge and the bits are held between edges; with nothing patched the conversion runs continuously
Shifts the converted range to -5V to 5V in place of 0-10V
Carries 10V while that bit of the converted value is set and 0V while it is clear
Carries all eight bits of the converted value at once, one channel per bit, 10V for a set bit and 0V for a clear one
Maps an eight bit input to an eight bit output through a 256-value table, with twenty banks of tables to scan
Scans through the tables of the selected bank, crossfading between neighbouring tables, 0 to 100%
Sets the scan position, 0-10V across the bank, and overrides the Wave knob while a cable is patched
Shifts where the input value is read in the table, a full turn shifting by all 256 positions
Sets the shift, 0-10V across all 256 positions, and overrides the Phase knob while a cable is patched
Picks one of the twenty banks of tables, whose name is drawn in the display
Selects the bank, 0.5V per bank across the twenty, and overrides the bank selector while a cable is patched
Sets one bit of the input value, a voltage above 1V counting as a one and anything lower as a zero
Sets the whole input value, one channel per bit, a channel above 1V counting as a one
Carries 10V while that bit of the table value is set and 0V while it is clear
Carries all eight bits of the table value at once, one channel per bit
Note — the display draws the table currently selected and names its bank
MP8.notes: The README names the bank file res/rom_default.json; the code reads res/rom.json first and falls back to res/default_rom.json, which is the file the installed plugin ships. The installed default bank file holds twenty banks.

lines: Polyphonic truth table: four gate inputs pick one of sixteen cells, and that cell's state becomes the output
Read as the ones bit of the cell number, a voltage above 1V counting as a one
Read as the twos bit of the cell number, a voltage above 1V counting as a one
Read as the fours bit of the cell number, a voltage above 1V counting as a one
Read as the eights bit of the cell number, a voltage above 1V counting as a one

Eight channel polyphonic CV mixer, also usable as a digital to analogue converter for eight bits
Scales its channel from -100% to 100% before that channel is added to the mix
One of the eight inputs added into the mix, polyphonic and scaled by its own knob
The eight scaled inputs added together, with as many channels as the widest input
Eight channel voltage controlled CV mixer, with each channel put out on its own and all eight put out as a mix
One of the eight inputs, polyphonic, scaled by its own knob and its own modulation
Scales its channel from -100% to 100%
Its channel on its own, after the level knob and the modulation for that channel
Adds to the level of its channel, 10V shifting the level by a full 100% when the knob beside it is fully up
Attenuates the modulation input for its channel, 0 to 100%
Scales the mix from silence to full, 0 to 100%
The eight scaled channels added together and scaled by the Mix knob
Adds twelve polyphonic inputs, each one switched to add, to subtract or to be left out
One of the twelve inputs; the switch beside it sets whether it is added, subtracted or left out
Three way switch: minus subtracts its input from the sum, 0 leaves that input out, plus adds it; it starts on 0
The inputs that are switched in, added together, with as many channels as the widest input
Expander that makes a second sum from the twelve inputs patched into Sum; it goes immediately to the right of Sum, and another SE can be chained to its right
Three way switch: minus subtracts that input of Sum from this sum, 0 leaves it out, plus adds it; it starts on 0
The inputs switched in here, added together, taken from the cables patched into Sum
Merges sixteen mono inputs into one polyphonic output, in 2HP
Feeds one channel of the polyphonic output; an input with no cable puts 0V on its channel
Carries the inputs as one polyphonic cable, each input on its own channel, with as many channels as the highest numbered input that has a cable
Splits a polyphonic input into sixteen mono outputs, in 2HP
The polyphonic cable that is split across the outputs, one channel to each
Carries one channel of the polyphonic input, and 0V where the input has no such channel
Merges sixteen stereo pairs into a left and a right polyphonic output, in 2HP
The left side of its pair, and with nothing patched into the right side of that pair it feeds both outputs
The right side of its pair
Carries the left inputs as one polyphonic cable, one channel per pair, with as many channels as the highest numbered pair whose left input has a cable
Carries the right inputs as one polyphonic cable, one channel per pair, with as many channels as the highest numbered pair whose left input has a cable
